extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, judges, and legal scholars handling news-agency litigation (preliminary injunctions, unfair competition/confidential-information disputes)
extracted.subtask_description: Supplemental defendant brief/answer in litigation between news agencies arguing legal standards for preliminary injunctions, equitable defenses (unclean hands, laches), the legal status of news/tips, and sufficiency of affidavit evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: News is public property and cannot be appropriated
rubrics_metrics.description: News is public property and cannot be appropriated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement asserted as a legal principle in defense: news as public property generally cannot be monopolized; but surrounding discussion qualifies when protection may attach (see other criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection terminates with publication
rubrics_metrics.description: While one gathering news may be entitled to certain protection therein, the right to this protection terminates with the publication of such news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to argue defendant may lawfully use news after it has been published by complainant's members (i.e., post-publication the gatherer's protective interest ends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal use bars complaint when gatherer avails of others
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a gatherer of news is shown to be engaged in availing itself of the product of the energies of other news gatherers it cannot be heard to complain if such others avail themselves of the products of its labors (122 Fed. Rep. 794).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If complainant itself uses news gathered by others, that conduct weakens or defeats its equitable claim against defendant for similar conduct; invoked as a defense (unclean hands theme).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclean hands defeats equitable relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The proofs before the Court disclose beyond a pre-adventure that complainant's hands are not only not clean, but on the contrary are thoroughly unclean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If complainant has purloined defendant's news (evidence of which defendant claims exists), complainant is not entitled to equitable relief such as an injunction; applies across classes of news taken by the same means/source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for issuing a preliminary injunction (Truly v. Wanger)
rubrics_metrics.description: The issuance of preliminary injunction is a matter resting within the sound discretion of the Court; this discretion should not be exercised in favor of granting the injunction, except in a case where the right is clear, and the injury impending and threatened so as to be averted only by the issuance of an injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court should require clear right and imminent irreparable injury that only an injunction can prevent. Quoted: 'The right must be clear, the injury impending, and threatened so as to be averted only by the preventative process of an injunction.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay/laches undermines claim to irreparable injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Having uncomplainingly suffered this 'irreparable damage' for eighteen months, should not the complainant now wait until the defendant can have its day in Court ... ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long, unexplained delay in seeking injunctive relief suggests absence of urgent irreparable harm and counsels against issuing a preliminary injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and quality of evidence on application for temporary injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon an application for a temporary injunction the proofs should clearly establish a situation warranting interference by the Court to prevent irreparable injury. No such injury is shown. The complainant's affidavits ... do not approach the dignity of evidence. They are a tissue of hearsay, assumptions and conjectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits based on hearsay, conjecture, or interested witnesses are insufficient to support an injunction; court should not predetermine contested facts absent strong admissible proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and proprietary value of a 'tip' / 'scoop' / 'beat'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'tip' may perhaps be defined as such an outline of the main features of a news event as to enable a person ... to identify the event and to locate the place of its origin, thus enabling verification and amplification. If one news agency had on its wires an important story ... the purloining of that information would enable an agency so purloining it to report to its customers a story which otherwise they would not have received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'tip' or 'scoop' has proprietary value to the gatherer because it yields exclusive/timely publication advantages; protection arguments treat purloining a tip as appropriation of that value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purloining a 'tip' is as stealing of confidential property (pre-publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purloining of a 'tip' of an item of important news (in the nature of a 'beat' or 'scoop') is, in principle, as much the stealing of confidential property as though the whole text of the story were taken...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When information is held in confidence prior to publication, misappropriation of even outlines/tips can constitute actionable appropriation; emphasis is on secrecy/confidential proprietary interest pre-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of equities and harm to defendant's business/goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court ... should not make an order so destructive of defendant's business and good will ... upon affidavit evidence of the kind that has been presented here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deciding injunctive relief, consider the destructive effect on defendant's business, reputation and goodwill; an injunction's potential harm weighs against issuance absent clear necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate remedy at law bars equitable injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: For each and every of the alleged injuries, or threatened injuries set forth in the complaint, the complainant has a complete and adequate remedy at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If damages or other legal remedies suffice, equitable relief like an injunction is not appropriate; defendant pleads this as a separate defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry custom: obtaining and re-writing items from other newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a well known and practically universal custom for publishers of newspapers ... to obtain and read editions of newspapers published by others ... and for such publishers ... to re-write such items of news therein contained ... and to publish the same, sometimes with and sometimes without additional verification, and without revealing the original source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customary practices of publishers and agencies (reading others' papers and re-writing items) undermine claims that such practices are wrongful per se; context and confidentiality agreements matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality/understanding with subscribers as basis for proprietary interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Such information or news is so furnished to such subscribers under an express understanding and agreement with such subscribers that the same will not be furnished or communicated by them to any other person ... and that it will remain confidential and secret until it has been regularly published by them ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an agency furnishes news to subscribers under express agreements of confidentiality until publication, that creates a proprietary interest that may support equitable relief if breached — but defendant asserts complainant lacks such consistent practice here.
